title: epipactis helleborine var. herbacea
intro: Epipactis helleborine var. herbacea, commonly known as the wood-sorrel orchid or European helleborine, is a rare and endangered orchid species native to Europe and Asia. The plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its potential health benefits, including the ability to treat respiratory issues, fever, and skin conditions. The therapeutic actions of Epipactis helleborine var. herbacea are attributed to its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties, which help to soothe and protect the body from infections and diseases. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are being studied for their potential to treat various health conditions.
